title: Reliability Collaboration: SLO Experiment Grid & Cross-Team Runbook
body:
Purpose and context:
This is a working runbook for running a set of small, fast experiments that validate SLO thresholds, SLA mappings, and staggered rollout patterns across Redwood’s serving runtime and hosted API. The goal is not to design one monolithic SLO policy but to create an experiment grid that surfaces trade-offs between latency P95, request-level quality regressions, and token cost under production-like load.

Audience:
- Primary: SREs, serving-runtime engineers, product owners for Hosted API
- Secondary: Solutions Eng, Observability, Product (Dedicated & Private planners)

High-level objectives:
1) Create 6 reproducible experiments (see grid) that exercise realistic workload mixes (chat, streaming, embeddings).
2) Validate three candidate SLO tiers for latency (P50/P95) and availability tied to error-budget burn patterns.
3) Produce a staged rollout plan (dark -> canary -> graduated rollout) that maps to Dedicated/Hosted/Private environments.
4) Capture operational runbooks for rollback and mitigation that any oncall can execute within 15 minutes.

Success metrics (what "done" looks like):
- Experiment artifacts: load scripts, baseline traces, and a one-page summary per experiment (6 pages).
- Confirmed SLO thresholds for at least two product routes with documented unit-cost delta < 15% versus baseline.
- Rollout playbook validated in staging and used for a real canary deployment on Hosted API.
- Post-experiment retro with action items and a prioritized backlog for Product/Optimize team.

Experiment grid (quick reference):
Columns = workload mix, traffic profile, kernel/quantization variant, primary metric, secondary metrics, failure mode simulated
1) Chat short-turns (burst traffic), host-model (non-quantized) -> primary P95 latency, sec: token cost, failure: instance OOM
2) Chat long-turns (KV-heavy), quantized-int8 -> primary throughput, sec: quality drift (BLEU/embedding-similarity), failure: KV cache thrash
3) Streaming partial responses, mixed traffic -> primary time-to-first-byte, sec: request success rate, failure: partial stream interruptions
4) Embeddings high-concurrency -> primary per-embedding latency tail, sec: CPU/GPU utilization, failure: queue growth/backpressure
5) Reranking (short inputs + large model) -> primary latency, sec: model accuracy on eval set, failure: slow kernels / CPU fallback
6) Mixed client profile (PLG traffic sample) -> primary error-budget burn rate, sec: overall costs, failure: cascading fallbacks

Quick design notes:
- Each experiment must include: workload generator script (k6/locust wrapper), a baseline run, an intervention run (change SLO, enable caching, change batching config), and a controlled "fault" injection (30s network jitter or instance restart).
- Keep runs under 90 minutes to encourage iteration.
- Use the staging Dedicated cluster for interventions that change kernel or quantization; use Hosted sandbox for client-level experiments.

Stakeholders and roles:
- Experiment lead (owner, runs the experiment): Arjun Patel
- Observability & metrics: Lena Ortiz (dashboarding, alert tuning)
- Serving runtime config & kernel changes: Tomás Ruiz
- Product mapping & SLA translation: Priya Nair
- Oncall / mitigation lead: Samir Khan
- Reviewer / PM reviewer: Maya Chen (doc owner)

Timeline (working sprint-by-sprint):
- Week 0 (Preparation, 1 week): finalize grid, create load scripts, reserve staging capacity.
- Week 1 (Baseline runs, 1 week): run baseline for all 6 experiments, collect traces and outputs.
- Week 2 (Intervention runs, 1 week): execute interventions, collect cost+quality metrics.
- Week 3 (Rollout rehearsal, 1 week): run dark canaries + rollback drills; validate runbook steps.
- Week 4 (Retro + decision): consolidate findings, recommend SLO thresholds, prioritize follow-ups.

Staggered rollout pattern (recommended):
1) Dark launch: route 5% mirrored traffic from Hosted to target variant (no client side exposure) for 24–72h. Check traces and similarity metrics.
2) Canary: 1% live traffic for 2h, 5% for 6h, 10% for 24h if error-budget burn < X.
3) Gradual rollout: double traffic every 6h while monitoring SLOs and operator gates; abort if burn exceeds triggers.

Operator gates and automatic abort conditions:
- If P95 latency > configured threshold for 2 consecutive 10-minute windows -> automatic rollback to previous model variant.
- If error-budget burn rate exceeds 3x expected in a 30-minute window -> scale down rollout or pause.
- If observed quality regression on eval prompts crosses 4% delta -> stop and tag the change as a quality incident.

Runbook (quick play):
- Pre-checks: validate feature flags, confirm rollback image available, ensure metrics dashboards open, notify oncall.
- Abort steps: 1) toggle feature flag off; 2) route traffic to fallback variant; 3) scale up fallback capacity if needed; 4) collect traces and create incident ticket with tags (sre, rollout, priority-1).
- Post-abort: capture a postmortem note and re-run the failed experiment in isolated mode.

Risks and mitigations:
- Seeding noisy signals from synthetic load -> mitigate by using PLG production trace replay for at least one experiment.
- Cost blowout during intervention -> cap staging cluster spend and set automated budget alarms.
- Customer-visible regressions -> always start with dark mirroring, never with immediate live traffic.

Telemetry and dashboards:
- Baseline dashboard name: SLO-Experiment-Baseline (create under Observability folder).
- Required panels: P50/P95/P99 latency, token-per-request cost, request success rate, error-budget burn curves, kernel fallback counters, GPU util, queue depth.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Should we include Dedicated-only SLO tiers that differ for private deployments? (decision owner: Priya)
- Exact error-budget formula for streaming routes (do we weight partial responses?) (owner: Lena)
- Target thresholds for P95 for embeddings vs chat (owner: Product)

Action items (first sprint):
- Arjun: deliver all k6 scripts and README by 2026-01-19.
- Lena: create baseline dashboard and wire alerts by 2026-01-20.
- Tomás: provision staging Dedicated nodes with both quantized and non-quantized kernels by 2026-01-18.
- Priya: map two Hosted API routes to SLO tiers and update SLA doc by 2026-01-21.
- Maya: schedule review session with Product and Solutions Eng for 2026-01-22.

Notes to self / informal:
- Keep experiment runs short and iterative; avoid trying to answer every question in one run.
- Record short Loom walkthroughs for each experiment setup so new SREs can reproduce.
- Use the "experiment" label on all Jira tickets created as part of this plan.

Appendix (examples of quick checks to run before starting an experiment):
- kubectl get pods -n staging -o wide | grep serving
- curl -H 'x-experiment: true' https://staging-hosted.redwood/v1/health
- Small smoke: run 50 reqs at concurrency 4 for 2 minutes and check P95

Revision history:
- 2026-01-12 created by Maya Chen
- 2026-01-18 Tomás added staging provisioning notes
- 2026-02-15 Lena updated dashboard requirements after preliminary baseline
- 2026-02-22 doc updated to include rollout gate thresholds (current)

Unresolved: pending Product decision on exact threshold values for Hosted API chat routes.

End of runbook (working doc).
